h.3d5ee30c: When you move, adrenaline speeds up the heart and the pulse rises with effort. That is what the 'heart rate zones' on watches and machines are based on.
h.ce775240: Your medication dampens that signal: the pulse rises less than normal for the same effort (with beta-blockers, about 20 or 30 beats fewer).
h.0e443ad0: Your muscles work just the same. If you chase the watch's heart rate zone, you will end up making considerably more effort than you should.
h.3b5fa206: Go by your breathing: you should be able to talk in short sentences, but not sing. This is the talk test, and it works with any medication.
h.aaa1b588: Use how hard the effort feels (Borg scale) or the talk test, not maximum heart rate formulas or the zones on the watch.
h.916cd367: Warm up and cool down for 5–10 minutes: with the pulse held back, the body takes longer to adapt.
h.c637ec83: Dizziness, breathlessness that does not improve when you stop or a very slow pulse with symptoms: stop and seek advice.
h.d269a207: Why can exercise lower your blood sugar?
h.366f0c81: Sugar (glucose) travels in the blood and is the fuel for the muscles.
h.4eaefb12: When you move, the muscles take it from the blood by themselves, even if there is little insulin. That is why exercise lowers blood sugar.
h.f8ff7a5c: Your medication lowers it too. The two add up and a low can come during exercise or up to 24 hours later, even at night.
h.780fe6f2: With a simple plan you can train safely: measure beforehand, carry fast-acting sugar and, if you notice a low, stop and take 15 g.
h.dc10ac1b: Measure your glucose before training and, on days with long or intense sessions, also before going to bed.
h.929c721b: Always carry fast-acting sugar (sachets, glucose or juice); if you train alone, tell someone.
h.c13fa668: Signs of a low: cold sweat, tremor, sudden hunger or confusion. With a beta-blocker, tremor and palpitations may not warn you; sweating does.
h.bf780ab4: If lows keep happening on exercise days, talk to your doctor about adjusting the dose.
h.b58e211b: Why do you need to take care with knocks?
h.d56ba332: A knock breaks small blood vessels and a little blood leaks under the skin.
h.a55fd234: Normally platelets and clotting form a plug within a few minutes and a small bruise is left.
h.161f9144: Your medication makes the plug take longer to form: bruises are bigger and a hard knock can bleed internally.
h.ae0d7fc5: Exercise is indicated; what changes is avoiding knocks and falls. That is why balance is so important for you.
h.25b84809: Avoid contact sports and activities with a risk of falling at speed.
h.f4312945: Train balance 2–3 times a week, with a support within reach.
h.c52c7543: A blow to the head even if it seems minor, large bruises without a knock, blood in the urine or black stools: go to the emergency department.
h.f70edc4b: Why can you feel dizzy on standing up or when you finish?
h.9425bcd4: Sitting down, blood reaches the head without effort.
h.766ea98c: When you stand up, blood tends to drop to the legs. Your medication relaxes the blood vessels or lowers blood pressure, and the body takes longer to compensate.
h.0c21caa6: For a moment less blood reaches the head: dizziness, blurred vision or weakness. Something similar happens when you finish exercising: blood pressure stays lower for a few hours.
h.3553c724: It is avoided with slow changes: sit on the edge, wait a few seconds and stand up. And always finish by slowing down little by little.
h.aeecfb5e: Cool down for 5–10 minutes at the end, without stopping abruptly.
h.311db6dd: Get up slowly, especially when getting out of bed or after exercises on the floor.
h.b9f1ce66: Drink water and avoid training in the hours of peak effect of the dose and in the first days after a dose change.
h.3595a29f: If you often feel dizzy or actually faint, seek advice: a medicine may need adjusting.
h.04e9c571: Why do you need to look after water and salts?
h.1cdfb27a: Some medicines make the kidneys get rid of more water and salts; others, such as lithium, need you not to be short of water.
h.6a072f16: When you exercise you also lose water and salt in sweat. The two losses add up.
h.7ae52dce: If water or potassium runs short, dizziness, cramps, weakness or palpitations can appear, and the kidneys suffer.
h.99344404: The solution is to drink before you feel thirsty, also during and after exercise, and to choose the time well.
h.89a1b371: Drink before, during and after; in the heat or in long sessions, a little more. If your fluids are restricted because of your heart or kidneys, keep to the amount your doctor told you.
h.223bad5a: With strong diuretics (furosemide, torasemide), avoid training in the 2–4 hours after the dose.
h.58f0a173: Do not take anti-inflammatories (ibuprofen, naproxen…) for muscle soreness: with dehydration they can damage the kidneys.
h.14feb0cc: Frequent cramps, weakness or palpitations: mention it to your doctor (you may need a blood test). With lithium, seek advice if you notice tremor, diarrhoea or confusion.
h.c9902a29: Why do you tolerate heat less well?
h.f035e350: When you move, the body produces heat and gets rid of it by sweating and sending blood to the skin.
h.a1f2455e: Some medicines reduce sweating; others remove water or slow the flow of blood to the skin. Heat builds up sooner.
h.3eb4f6dc: Signs that you are overdoing it: headache, nausea, dizziness or hot, dry skin. If they appear, stop, find shade and cool down.
h.0ec2a43a: In the heat, train early in the day or in a cool indoor space, drink before you feel thirsty and lower the intensity.
h.1fa2987c: In summer, avoid the middle of the day; better early in the morning or somewhere air-conditioned.
h.fa8ed945: Drink before you feel thirsty (unless your fluids are restricted) and wear light clothing.
h.d8dcd1e8: Lower the intensity on hot or humid days: the same effort costs more.
h.18e1051a: Why does the risk of falls increase?
h.4f5d2afd: Keeping your balance is continuous work: the brain corrects every stumble in tenths of a second.
h.efcfa437: Your medication causes sleepiness, slows the reflexes or lowers blood pressure: that correction arrives later.
h.3ea5837b: A stumble that used to end in just a fright can end in a fall and, in older people, in a hip fracture.
h.419f34e3: The best antidote is to train balance and leg strength, always with a support within reach.
h.37df4717: Train balance 2–3 times a week next to a wall, a chair or a handrail.
h.27f15824: Do not train in the hours after a dose if it makes you sleepy.
h.7d624d09: Footwear with a firm sole, good light and no loose rugs.
h.a9a7dbb8: Talk to your doctor: sometimes a medicine that causes sleepiness can be reduced.
h.c64530be: How do you tell muscle soreness from a muscle problem?
h.99f35620: Normal muscle soreness appears after 24–48 hours, in the muscle that has worked, and goes in 2–4 days.
h.2747c1ca: With your medication the muscle may be somewhat more sensitive to new or very intense exercise. It is no reason not to train: you progress little by little.
h.1c9edc86: Pain all over the body or in muscles you have not worked, real weakness and dark urine are not normal. In that case, stop and seek advice.
h.803b6e09: Start with light loads in the first weeks, without going to failure, and increase when you can do it with good technique.
h.2e55fd5e: The first 2–3 weeks: light loads, few sets and no slow lowering with a lot of weight.
h.9b4277a0: Do not add new medicines without mentioning it: some antibiotics and antifungals raise the risk.
h.da17563d: Generalised pain, weakness or dark urine: seek advice; you may need a blood test (CK).
h.1eceee21: Why do the tendons need protecting?
h.10db1cc7: A tendon joins muscle to bone, like the Achilles at the heel. It is made of very strong fibres.
h.e9cf3267: Some medicines (antibiotics of the quinolone group and corticosteroids in long treatments) weaken those fibres.
h.a22cbfb4: A jump, a sprint or a sudden change of direction can then damage or rupture it, especially after the age of 60.
h.e10c2523: While the treatment lasts (with quinolones, 4 weeks more), choose non-impact activities: walking, cycling or swimming.
h.5246a5c0: Avoid jumps, hard running, sudden changes of direction and maximal loads.
h.d60f69af: If pain appears in the heel, calf, shoulder or elbow, stop and seek advice.
h.b921e1c1: With long-term corticosteroids strength work is highly recommended, but with slow progression and no explosive exercises.
h.6070691f: What is the 'QT' and why does it matter?
h.82c6e40f: With every beat, the heart is activated and then 'recharges'. On the electrocardiogram, that time is called the QT interval.
h.29ce9ff8: Some medicines lengthen the recharge. On its own it does not usually cause symptoms, but it leaves the heart more sensitive.
h.6bca1de6: The risk of arrhythmia rises when things add up: low potassium or magnesium, dehydration, a very slow pulse or another medicine that also lengthens the QT.
h.f42579ad: With moderate exercise and these precautions you can train safely. Let your doctor know if you notice palpitations or faint.
h.67b27959: Avoid stimulants: energy drinks, pre-workout supplements and decongestants.
h.ae928dde: Stay hydrated and, if you take diuretics, ask about checking your potassium and magnesium.
h.c04dbe40: Palpitations that do not settle, severe dizziness or fainting: stop and seek advice (you may need an electrocardiogram).
h.e8f53888: Why does your heart speed up?
h.95a74d64: At rest, the heart beats at a calm rate and speeds up with effort.
h.7cb33bf2: Your medication stimulates it: the pulse is faster at rest and rises more than the effort calls for.
h.c47418d8: You may notice palpitations or tremor, and the watch will tell you that you are working harder than you really are.
h.cd591a70: Go by how hard the effort feels, lower the intensity if you notice palpitations and do not add other stimulants.
h.d4b307bb: Intensity by how hard the effort feels or the talk test, not by pulse.
h.23ed8b08: Avoid too much coffee, energy drinks, pre-workout supplements and decongestants.
h.a212ae91: Palpitations that last minutes, with dizziness or with chest pain: stop and seek advice.
h.327a55f9: Why is strength work your best ally?
h.05f1ec6a: Some treatments promote muscle loss or weakening of the bone (long-term corticosteroids, some medicines for weight loss or for prostate cancer).
h.4e36e9b4: Strength training sends the opposite signal: muscle is maintained or grows and bone is strengthened.
h.4bc1a900: It works with 2–3 sessions a week and enough protein at meals (unless your doctor has restricted it).
h.d17647f1: With more fragile bone, work on balance too so as not to fall, always with a support.
h.ca6dfa43: Strength work 2–3 days a week with the large muscle groups (legs, back, pushing).
h.39addeda: Progress little by little and with no jumps if the bone is weak.
h.a9216429: Protein at every meal: pulses, egg, dairy, fish or meat.
h.7bc41beb: Why do you burn sooner in the sun?
h.cf3f0c30: The sun reaches the skin and, given time, reddens it.
h.35843cab: Your medication makes the skin more sensitive to light: you burn sooner and with less sun, even on cloudy days.
h.346fb450: Protect yourself: a cap or hat, clothing that covers you and high-factor sunscreen.
h.615321f8: Choose early morning or late evening, or train in the shade.
h.62d73f9a: Factor 50 sunscreen and clothing that covers you if you train outdoors.
h.a0a05aa4: Avoid the middle of the day.
h.3d24060e: If a rash or a burn appears with little sun, seek advice.
h.963de852: Why do you need to watch your blood pressure during strength work?
h.7cb2fc1c: Your medication can raise blood pressure.
h.aef38e7f: If you hold your breath while straining (what is called the Valsalva manoeuvre), blood pressure shoots up for a few seconds.
h.34d1f881: Breathing continuously (breathing out as you push), the rise is much smaller.
h.54beb7b0: Measure your blood pressure: with 180/110 or more at rest, do not train until it is under control; with 160/100 or more, only light to moderate intensity until the treatment is adjusted.
h.cd89d811: Always breathe during strength work; avoid maximal loads and sustained efforts without moving.
h.9a9cba35: Measure your blood pressure at rest from time to time and note it in the diary.
h.6691528b: Severe headache, chest pain or blurred vision with effort: stop and seek advice.
h.702eb480: Some treatments cause tiredness or reduce exercise capacity: the same walk takes more out of you.
h.21590a68: It is not a lack of willpower: the body has less in reserve. If you push as before, the tiredness builds up.
h.9fe5370f: Find your best time of day and prefer shorter, more frequent sessions.
h.b0e3aa27: Progress slowly and value consistency. If the tiredness is new or getting worse, mention it to your doctor.
h.48dfed7c: Go by how hard the effort feels, not by what you used to do.
h.f9e4e824: Several short sessions, of 10 minutes, also add up.
h.5237d8ba: New or severe tiredness, or tiredness that is getting worse: seek advice.
